 Elliot Raphaelson 
 By Elliot Raphaelson | The Savings Game PUBLISHED: October 23, 2026 at 5:25 PM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... For individuals who plan to enroll in Medicare for 2027, or who are already enrolled but wish to make changes, I highly recommend that you read the official government-issued handbook ”Medicare and You 2027.”
 The easiest way to access it is to type the title into the search field of an internet search engine such as Google. Likely the first link will be to a PDF document of the 128-page guide on the website medicare.gov.
 If you want a free physical copy of the handbook, contact the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) by calling 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227).
 Open enrollment began on October 15, and it ends December 7, so there is still time to study the guide, compare your current medical and drug benefits options for 2027, and weigh your options.
 During open enrollment, you can change your Medicare health benefits and drug coverage for 2027. You can join, switch, or drop Medicare Advantage plans or Medicare drug plans, or switch to Original Medicare.
 January 1, 2027 is the effective date for any changes you make in your health coverage or drug coverage. This is also the start date for health and drug coverage for 2027, if you did not make any changes in coverage.
 Another enrollment period to note, Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment, runs from January 1 to March 31, 2027, and only applies if you are already enrolled in a Medicare Advantage Plan. During this period, you can make one single switch to a different Medicare Advantage Plan or to Original Medicare. Any changes you make will be effective the first day of the month after the Plan receives your change request.
 During this period, you cannot switch from Original Medicare to a Medicare Advantage Plan. If you are in Original Medicare, you cannot join a Medicare drug plan, or switch from one Medicare drug plan to another.
 In a recent article in Barron’s, Elizabeth O’Brien discussed the likely changes associated with Medicare enrollment. She pointed out that in the annual open enrollment period, beneficiaries will likely find fewer options because many carriers will be “scaling back” their offerings, especially Medicare Advantage plans.
 About 3.2 million individuals are in Medicare Advantage plans that will be discontinued in 2027, according to CNN reporting. According to KFF, a nonpartisan health-care research nonprofit, the number of stand-alone drug plans in 2027 will fall from 360 to 316 in 2027.
 Most Medicare recipients will have several options to choose from. Through December 7, beneficiaries can select a Part D drug plan, a new Medicare Advantage plan, or switch from Original Medicare plan to an Advantage Plan, or vice versa. Medicare supplemental policies are largely regulated at the state level, and are not part of open enrollment.
 Beneficiaries should have already been notified an Annual Notice of Change from their provider, outlining changes effective on January 1, 2027. If you have received that notice, you should be researching your 2027 options on the plan finder tool option at Medicare.com.
 According to KFF, Medicare Advantage now enrolls approximately 35 million individuals which represents approximately 55% of the Medicare population. Humana has stated that about 600,000 members, nearly 9% of its membership will be affected by plan exits in 2027. In addition, United Healthcare and CVS will also be terminating plans.
 According to CMS, the weighted average monthly premiums across Medicare Advantage plans is projected to decrease 16.5% next year. However, you have to look at the cost of copayments, coinsurance and deductibles to determine the total monthly cost. Your plan may include extras such as gym membership and other perks. However, far more important is whether your existing doctors will accept insurance from your provider.
 If you are considering leaving a Medicare Advantage plan for Original Medicare, make sure you understand the cost of a supplemental insurance plan (aka Medigap) that covers copays and some of the co-insurance that Medicare does not cover, and make sure you understand your state’s rules on Medigap coverage (they vary!).
 Before you make a final decision regarding new coverage, you should consider using the free services of your State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP). For more information, contact SHIP at shiphelp.org or 1-877-839-2675. Their site also has a helpful FAQ section.
 Elliot Raphaelson welcomes your questions and comments at raphelliot@gmail.com.
